task.description: Independently gate §11.10 (six subsections, §11.10.0-§11.10.6) of lib/letflow/design/iss0113-tenant-fixture-sandbox-restore-opt-in.md against step-11's own task.acceptance_criteria, re-deriving every claim from source rather than trusting CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary.
acceptance_criteria: Re-derive from ExUnit's and DBConnection.Ownership's actual documented/source semantics that on_exit runs after the owning process exits, and that with_provisioning_repo/1 called from the on_exit process has no problematic interaction with the original test's gone {:shared, self()} registration
Confirm teardown/2's actual body only needs tenant_id/schema_name plus a live, permissioned connection -- not the same connection provisioning used
Confirm the :exit-catching hardening in guarded/2/log_teardown/3 is correctly scoped as defense-in-depth, not a mask for the fix not working
Confirm the post-teardown verification requirement is concrete enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement without guessing
No implementation code present in the design

result.summary:
PASS on all five checks. Re-derived, not inherited:

1. ON_EXIT TIMING/OWNERSHIP -- confirmed against the actually-installed toolchain's own compiled docs, not the design's narrative: `Code.fetch_docs(ExUnit.Callbacks)` for `on_exit/2` states verbatim 'executed in a blocking fashion after the test exits' and 'executed in a different process than the test process' -- exactly the premise §11.10.0 rests its diagnosis on. Cross-checked against deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/adapters/sql/sandbox.ex's own 'owner exited' FAQ section (lines 167-227, read in full): confirms the symptom is specifically 'the test process has finished... [the owner] no longer exists... Ecto will check the connection back in and notify the client process' -- matches the BLOCKER's exact stack trace shape. Checked DBConnection.Ownership.Manager (deps/db_connection/lib/db_connection/ownership/manager.ex): it is a GenServer started once per pool inside its own `init/1` (`DBConnection.start_link(module, pool_opts)`), confirming the design's 'one manager per pool, one pool per Ecto.Repo' claim from source rather than from ProvisioningRepo's own moduledoc alone -- so with_provisioning_repo/1's Sandbox.mode(ProvisioningRepo, :auto) call structurally cannot touch Letflow.Repo's owners, and running it from the on_exit process (a different process from the original owner) is not a problem because :auto mode is not owner-scoped the way {:shared, pid} is -- it performs a per-query auto-checkout regardless of caller identity, confirmed by reading with_provisioning_repo/1's own body (tenant_fixture.ex:332-342): no explicit checkout/allow call, no dependency on any specific process being alive. Fully orthogonal to the original test's now-invalid {:shared, self()} registration, as claimed.

2. TEARDOWN/2 CONNECTION INDEPENDENCE -- read teardown/2's actual body (tenant_fixture.ex:522-534): TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1 (checked further -- lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex:166-171 -- is PURE, `Ecto.UUID.cast/1` plus string concatenation, zero I/O, even stronger than the design's claim of 'a Repo.get_by read'; the design's own prose at §11.10.2 slightly overstates this by calling it a query, but this only strengthens the conclusion, it does not weaken it), then `Repo.query!(DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE)` and two `Repo.delete_all` calls, all keyed by tenant_id/schema_name already closed over in the on_exit closure. Nothing reads in-transaction/uncommitted state from a specific connection. Confirms design's conclusion: teardown needs a live, permissioned connection to the same database, not the specific connection provisioning used -- verified against the actual code, not asserted.

3. :EXIT HARDENING SCOPE -- confirmed correctly scoped as defense-in-depth. §11.10.1 explicitly separates the two defects (connection unusable = root cause; rescue-only boundary = independently real but insufficient alone) and §11.10.3 states plainly that §11.10.2 alone closes the BLOCKER under normal operation, with the :exit catch guarding a 'currently-hypothetical' future scenario. Critically, §11.10.5 item 4 and §11.10.3's closing paragraph explicitly keep teardown/2's own DROP SCHEMA/delete_all statements UNWRAPPED by any guarded/2-style boundary, with a stated reason (load-bearing cleanup must fail loudly, silently swallowing it would orphan schemas/rows -- worse than today). This is the correct discipline: the hardening cannot mask the fix not working, because the fix's success criterion (§11.10.4 item 2) is verified by direct post-condition queries, not by the absence of a raised exit.

4. POST-TEARDOWN VERIFICATION CONCRETENESS -- §11.10.4 item 2 names exact, executable checks: a SELECT-equivalent against information_schema.schemata (or the existing schema_present?/1 oracle) for schema absence, plus Repo.get_by(Registration, tenant_id: ...) and Repo.get(Tenant, tenant_id) both returning nil for row absence -- and correctly sequences this as a SEPARATE test running after the teardown-exercising test in the same file, citing ExUnit's own sync-queue ordering (on_exit for test N fires before test N+1 starts) as why this is safe to assert without a race. Item 3 additionally requires confirming the widened boundary doesn't swallow a genuine cleanup failure. This is unambiguous and directly implementable without further judgement calls.

5. NO IMPLEMENTATION CODE -- grepped the full design file for fenced code blocks (```elixir/```ex): zero matches. All shape descriptions (the on_exit closure shape, the try/rescue/catch expansion) are inline prose fragments describing signatures/structure, consistent with every other gated section in this same file (§11.6, §10.3.2, etc.), not pasted implementation bodies.

Non-blocking note recorded, not a failure: §11.10.2's inline 'Concretely:' example omits the `teardown_wrap` binding name that §11.10.5 (the authoritative implementation subsection) correctly specifies -- harmless, since §11.10.5 is unambiguous on its own and ELIXIR-DEV implements from it.

Also verified the rework_count/max_rework overage step-11 itself flagged (rework_count 4 > max_rework 3) is ORCH's/ORCHESTRATOR.md §5's call, not this gate's -- correctly not resolved unilaterally by CODE-DESIGNER, and not this validator's checklist item either (design-content gate only). Restating it here so it is not lost between handoffs.
